name: Hordeum
look_here_first: LITTLE BARLEY: native North American short-lived cool-season grass with a compact, erect, bristly BARLEY spike. Each rachis node contains THREE closely grouped spikelets (central + two lateral), whose narrow awns form a small bottlebrush. Magnify one node to distinguish introduced foxtail barley or wall barley, and examine the annual rooted crown.

comparison_lesson.memory_rule: LITTLE BARLEY: native North American short-lived cool-season grass with a compact, erect, bristly BARLEY spike. Each rachis node contains THREE closely grouped spikelets (central + two lateral), whose narrow awns form a small bottlebrush. Magnify one node to distinguish introduced foxtail barley or wall barley, and examine the annual rooted crown.
quick_split: Secale cereale also has a cereal spike but typically bears solitary paired-arranged spikelets (not Hordeum's distinctive triads) at rachis nodes; Hordeum murinum often has broader fanlike awned spikelet groups and is introduced. Cultivated barley Hordeum vulgare is larger and more robust; verify scale and individual spikelet arrangement.
comparison_lesson.guardrail: Potential lookalike taxa are references only; not newly admitted canonical species.
